summary:
Mission Nova is an interactive space exploration and astronaut training platform designed to make space science engaging, educational, and accessible for young learners. It transforms traditional space learning into an immersive, story-driven experience where users can explore the universe and train like junior astronauts.
The Solar System Explorer features all eight planets, Pluto, and the Moon, allowing learners to discover planetary information, interesting facts, and unique characteristics. Users can also explore Earth from above and access NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day to discover fascinating astronomical visuals.
The platform offers interactive Moon and Mars missions where learners experience astronaut challenges involving resource management, fuel, food, water, spacecraft stage separation, atmospheric layers, and lunar survival. Other celestial bodies provide educational exploration and information.
Guided by Commander Mira through voice and subtitles, learners progress through missions at their own pace, experiencing stories and realistic space scenarios before testing their knowledge through interactive quizzes.
With its engaging visuals, interactive 3D environments, and beginner-friendly approach, Mission Nova aims to inspire curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and introduce the next generation to the wonders and challenges of space exploration.
details:
Mission Nova is an interactive space exploration and astronaut training platform designed for young learners.

Users can also participate in interactive Moon and Mars missions, where they experience astronaut challenges involving fuel, food, water, spacecraft separation, atmospheric layers, and lunar survival. Commander Mira guides learners through missions using voice and subtitles.

Its major benefits include:

  • Encourages curiosity about astronomy and space science.
  • Provides interactive 3D exploration of celestial bodies.
  • Develops problem-solving and critical-thinking skills through mission challenges.
  • Introduces real astronaut responsibilities and resource management.
  • Supports learning through voice guidance, subtitles, and visual storytelling.
  • Makes complex space concepts easier for beginners to understand.

The intended impact of Mission Nova is to inspire the next generation of space explorers, scientists, and innovators by making space education more immersive and approachable.

The project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical space education and practical understanding by allowing learners to experience simulated astronaut missions and explore celestial environments.

It encourages scientific curiosity, independent learning, problem-solving, and interest in STEM fields. Ultimately, Mission Nova aims to make space exploration accessible to young learners and help them develop a deeper appreciation of our universe.

Mission Nova was developed using web technologies and interactive 3D development tools.

Technologies and tools:

  • HTML5 – Structure of the website.
  • CSS3 – Styling, layouts, animations, and visual design.
  • JavaScript – Interactive functionality and mission logic.
  • Three.js – Interactive 3D environments and Solar System visualization.
  • NASA APIs – Access to astronomy-related information and imagery, including the Astronomy Picture of the Day, where integrated.
  • VS Code – Development environment.
  • Web Browser – Testing and running the application.

Hardware: A standard computer or laptop was used for development and testing. No specialized hardware was required.

Instead of simply presenting information about planets, it allows learners to explore an interactive 3D Solar System and participate in simulated Moon and Mars missions.

A unique feature is Commander Mira, who guides learners through missions using voice and subtitles, creating a more immersive experience. The platform also combines educational facts, real astronomical imagery, resource-management challenges, and mission-based learning.

Its story-first approach allows learners to understand concepts through exploration and experience before testing their knowledge through quizzes. This makes space education feel less like studying and more like becoming a junior astronaut.

While developing Mission Nova, our team considered several important factors:

  • Target audience: Designed to be beginner-friendly and engaging for young learners.
  • Educational value: Ensuring that exploration and missions provide meaningful scientific learning.
  • User experience: Simple navigation, interactive elements, and an intuitive interface.
  • Scientific accuracy: Using credible space-related information and NASA resources where applicable.
  • Accessibility: Incorporating voice guidance, subtitles, and browser-based access.
  • Performance: Keeping the experience smooth and compatible with standard computers.
  • Engagement: Using storytelling, 3D visualization, and mission challenges to maintain interest.
  • Learning effectiveness: Allowing learners to understand concepts through exploration before attempting quizzes.
